title: HHT project manifest
description: Machine-readable configuration for one HHT repository. It holds only the facts that differ between repositories: identity, work tracker, documentation locations, and Git workflow. Anything identical in every repository is a constant held by the skill that owns it, not a field here. The nearest hhtproject.json up the directory tree wins, which is what makes a monorepo work.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema, so an editor can validate the manifest while it is being written. It is the one key allowed outside the schema's own properties.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this manifest format. A reader checks it before anything else, so a manifest written by a newer hht is reported as a version mismatch rather than as a list of unknown keys.

repository.description: Source repository as owner/name on GitHub, for example hedgehogtech/hht-marketplace.

projectType.description: What kind of engineering this repository holds. It is a human record and the setup-time switch for which sections get written; nothing reads it at runtime.

disciplines.description: Engineering disciplines this repository includes. Required and non-empty only when projectType is multidisciplinary; an empty array everywhere else.

items.description: One engineering discipline included in this repository.

harnesses.description: Agent harnesses configured for this repository. Each one has its own always-loaded instruction file, CLAUDE.md for claude and AGENTS.md for codex.

tracker.description: Where work items live. Required when the project includes software, and absent otherwise, because a repository with no software work has no implementation tickets to route.

kind.description: Which tracker holds work items: jira for an HHT Jira project, local for one file per work item in tasksSubfolder in the repository.

tasksSubfolder.description: Folder holding one file per work item, as a path under the local documentation entry's rootFolder that defaults to tasks/, so docs/tasks/ when nothing else is set. Only for kind local.

site.description: Atlassian site URL hosting the Jira project. Required for kind jira.

projectKey.description: Jira project key, for example HHTAI. Required for kind jira.

projectId.description: Numeric Jira project ID as a string. Required for kind jira, because a key can be renamed and an ID cannot.

boardId.description: Numeric Jira board ID as a string. A board is a view and can span projects, so it never identifies the project on its own. Required for kind jira.

issueTypes.description: Jira issue type IDs for this project. HHT uses standard types only and never creates subtasks. Required for kind jira.

epic.description: Issue type ID for an Epic, the parent of an approved specification's implementation work.

task.description: Issue type ID for a Task, used for implementation and decision tickets.

bug.description: Issue type ID for a Bug.

documentation.description: Where this repository's documents live. Exactly one entry is kind local, the repository tree the workflow skills write and read. Every other entry is a Confluence mirror of it. All entries are synced, so a document published from the repository goes to each mirror, not to one chosen among them. Every folder is a subfolder of the entry's rootFolder, and a local entry that names none is the docs/ tree.

items.description: One documentation location: the repository tree, or a Confluence space and the folders in it.

kind.description: Which store the entry names: local for folders in this repository, confluence for a Confluence space.

rootFolder.description: The folder every subfolder is under. For kind local, a repository-relative folder that defaults to docs/. For kind confluence, the numeric content ID, as a string, of the folder in the space, and required.

specsSubfolder.description: Where specifications go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to specs/. For kind local, repository folder names, where to-spec writes and to-plan reads. For kind confluence, the titles of nested Confluence folders, which receive the published copy.

plansSubfolder.description: Where plans go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to plans/. For kind local, repository folder names, where to-plan writes. For kind confluence, the titles of nested Confluence folders, which receive the published copy.

designsSubfolder.description: Where design documents go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to designs/. For kind local, repository folder names, where hht-style-design-doc writes. For kind confluence, the titles of nested Confluence folders, which receive the published copy.

decisionsSubfolder.description: Where decision records go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to decisions/. For kind local, repository folder names, where domain-modeling writes. For kind confluence, the titles of nested Confluence folders, which receive the published copy.

researchSubfolder.description: Where research notes go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to research/. Repository folder names, where research writes. Only for kind local: these notes are not published.

ideasSubfolder.description: Where refined ideas go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to ideas/. Repository folder names, where idea-refine writes. Only for kind local: these notes are not published.

outOfScopeSubfolder.description: Where out-of-scope notes go, as a path under rootFolder that defaults to out-of-scope/. Repository folder names, where triage writes. Only for kind local: these notes are not published.

site.description: Atlassian site URL hosting the Confluence space, for example https://hedgehogtech-team-001.atlassian.net. Required for kind confluence.

spaceKey.description: Confluence space key, for example HHT: ASCII letters and digits, with a leading tilde for a personal space. Required for kind confluence.

allOf.description: A local entry names repository folders and carries no Confluence identifier.
A Confluence entry names its site, space, and root folder by content ID, its subfolders by title, and only the subfolders of documents that are published.

gitWorkflow.description: Which remote-visible Git actions an agent may take in this repository. The guardrail hook reads this section; a repository whose manifest is missing or unusable runs as solo.

preset.description: Autonomous push scope: solo for a personal repository, under which the agent commits and pushes each verified change on its own, and which a repository with no usable manifest also runs as; team for a Hedgehog internal repository; client for a repository a client or external party sees. Opening a pull request always asks, merging is always denied, and the only force-push permitted is --force-with-lease with --force-if-includes to a feature branch.

defaultBranch.description: Branch a clone checks out, for example main. It is always protected, so it must appear in protectedBranches.

protectedBranches.description: Integration branches nobody pushes to directly outside the solo preset. Listed explicitly rather than inferred, so the hook and the prose cannot disagree about what is protected. It must contain defaultBranch, which JSON Schema cannot express because it compares two instance locations, so the readers and check_sync.py enforce that one rule.

allOf.description: Multidisciplinary projects name the disciplines they include.
A project that includes software tracks work somewhere; one that does not has no tracker at all.
A Jira tracker carries the identifiers needed to reach the project and no folder; a local one carries none of the identifiers.
